commitResults.messageTitle: Add storing of inputs into list

commitResults.messageBody:
Tasks are stored only as descriptions, so Clammy cannot retain or
display completion state.

Add a Task model that owns its description and done status. Support
mark and unmark commands and show status icons in list output.

Move the application into the clammy package to follow project coding
standards, and remove the unused Duke entry point.

Agents need consistent student context and project-level conventions
for Java and Git changes.

Set beginner defaults and add project skills that summarize the SE-EDU
Java and Git conventions. Mandate their use for future project work.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add task types and command parsing
commitResults.messageBody: Support todo, deadline, and event tasks with their corresponding command formats and display representations.
Record UI test cases in a shared test plan and require UI testing after code changes.

Clammy mixed input handling, command routing, task creation, task
mutation, and output in one large method. It also tracked the task
count in two places, allowing those values to drift apart.

Extract focused methods for each responsibility and keep taskCount as
the single source of truth. This improves readability and follows the
Single Level of Abstraction Principle while preserving visible
behavior.

Separate parsing, task storage, command handling, and console output so each component has a focused responsibility.\n\nAdd clearer validation and command guidance, allow flexible command input, and improve response spacing. Extend the UI test plan to cover the new behavior.

Represent malformed commands, unknown commands, and missing tasks with
specific checked exceptions. Catch their common ClammyException base at
the application boundary so recoverable errors keep the chatbot running.

Exercise every current malformed-command category and confirm that Clammy
continues accepting commands after each error. This guards the checked
exception flow and its specific correction messages against regressions.

Integrate the completed Level-5 exception hierarchy and its expanded UI
regression coverage while preserving the increment's branch history.

Group command handling, exceptions, tasks, and UI classes into focused
subpackages while retaining clammy.Clammy as the application entry point.

This makes responsibilities easier to locate without changing behavior.
